dedupe_keys.name: energystar more accurate and explainable building energy benchmarking

description: EnergyStar++ reproduces the ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager benchmarking models and proposes more accurate and explainable alternatives. The paper by Pandarasamy Arjunan, Kameshwar Poolla and Clayton Miller (arXiv 2019, revised June 2020) notes that the 1 to 100 ENERGY STAR score, used widely in the USA and Canada, rests on multiple linear regression; it tests regression with feature interactions and gradient boosted trees, which raise adjusted R2 by 4.9 and 24.9 per cent and cut normalised RMSE by 7.0 and 13.7 per cent on average across six building types, and uses SHAP values and force plots to show which attributes drive a building's score. The repository reproduces ENERGY STAR models for hotels, K-12 schools, multifamily housing, offices, retail stores and supermarkets, warehouses and worship facilities, includes an explanation app and studies public datasets for defining peer groups. Coverage: US building types covered by ENERGY STAR. Access: free code. Licence: MIT (SinBerBEST2 Lab and BUDS Group). Caveats: research code not maintained as a service, and training depends on public survey microdata. Simulation uses: benchmark models for school and other public building portfolios and for policy analysis of benchmarking scores. Related records: ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and the ALDI++ discord detection method.
